name: All Hands and Hearts (charityevals' estimate)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: US disaster response (muck and gut, mould sanitation, smoke remediation) and home repairs.
summary: All Hands and Hearts sends volunteers, led by its own staff, to US disasters to muck and gut flooded homes, sanitise them against mould, clean smoke-damaged houses after the Los Angeles fires and repair homes; its school rebuilds and relief abroad are a model of their own. The US work is modelled for the year to August 2025, the latest audited year: $9.2 million of its $11.2 million of cash programme spending (the split with the work abroad is our judgment, since the accounts give none), for about 800 muck and guts, 370 mould sanitations, 170 smoke-cleaned homes and an estimated 90 homes repaired, each valued at what a contractor would charge, on the site's log-income scale at the clients' consumption, with the volunteers' own wellbeing as a side effect (2%). The result, about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000 (0.0006 to 0.014), is low because the help goes to US households, whose consumption the site's log-income scale makes a dollar do little for, and because the volunteers' unpaid time (about 190,000 hours) and donated materials are much of what the work takes, so All Hands and Hearts' cash is credited with about half of it. Every branch is discounted for missing data: the counts are rounded, the homes repaired are our estimate and the value of the work to those served is a judgment. The biggest uncertainties are that value and what others would have done for the households anyway.

rows.label: Hours worked per volunteer
rows.explainer: Our judgment, with two anchors. Reference class: Team Rubicon's volunteers gave 47 hours each in 2024 (284,485 hours over about 6,000 deployed: its model), mostly on deployments of a week; All Hands and Hearts' volunteers live at its bases, are scheduled for up to two months at first, and its long-term volunteers paid a stipend stay for months (FAQ: allhandsandhearts.org/faqs, retrieved 2026-11-14), so more. Cross-check from the jobs: a muck and gut takes a crew of about six a day and a half (about 70 hours), a sanitation about 20, a smoke clean-up about 40 and a repaired home about 150, so the year's jobs take about 80,000 hours on site, 130,000 with travel, training, base duties and unfinished jobs, about 65 hours each. 90, from 40 to 200.

rows.label: Muck and guts of flooded homes in the US, over the year

source.title: All Hands and Hearts, Annual Report 2025: A Year in Review
source.quote: OVER THE PAST YEAR, ACROSS THE U.S., WE CONDUCTED: 800+ muck & guts 370+ mold sanitations

rows.explainer: Clearing a flooded home of mud, debris and its soaked contents, drywall, insulation and flooring, so that it can dry out. The report (November 2025) counts the year before it, about the fiscal year to August 2025. '800+' is the floor; the best guess a little above it, the high end allowing for the report's year reaching past August.

rows.label: Families returned home after smoke remediation, Los Angeles

source.title: All Hands and Hearts, Annual Report 2025: A Year in Review

rows.explainer: Homes left standing but unsafe after the January 2025 fires, cleaned of smoke residue, soot and ash with partner organisations (the Form 990's Los Angeles programme, $1,363,557).

rows.label: Homes repaired or rebuilt in the US, year to August 2025
rows.explainer: Our judgment: All Hands and Hearts publishes no count of repaired homes for the year. Its North Carolina plan is 'OVER THE NEXT 12 MONTHS WE WILL ASSIST 60 HOMEOWNERS WITH LONG-TERM RECOVERY' (insulation, drywall, flooring, doors, trim, paint: Form 990 Schedule O, line 4a); in Pasco County, Florida, contractors paid from grants did 'CRITICAL REPAIRS LIKE ROOF REBUILD OR HVAC AND ELECTRICAL WORK' (line 4b); Texas rebuilds began in the summer. Its Helene and Milton page counts '350+ homes supported', most of them muck and guts and sanitations counted above. 90, from 40 to 180.

rows.label: What a muck and gut would cost from a contractor
rows.explainer: Our judgment of what the household would pay a restoration contractor for the same work: removing flooded contents, cutting out drywall to above the flood line, pulling insulation and flooring, and drying the frame. Reference class: Angi's 2025 cost guide puts water-damage restoration at $3,822 on average, typically $1,361 to $6,282 (angi.com/articles/how-much-does-it-cost-repair-water-damage.htm, retrieved 2026-11-14), an average over all water-damage jobs, most of them smaller than a flooded floor gutted to the studs. $5,000, from $2,500 to $10,000.

rows.label: What a mould sanitation would cost from a contractor
rows.explainer: Our judgment, anchored on published cost guides: Angi gives mould removal an average of $2,225, Bob Vila $1,125 to $3,439 with an average of $2,254 (angi.com and bobvila.com cost guides, retrieved 2026-11-14). After a muck and gut the walls are open, which makes the job easier, but a flooded crawlspace and framing are a large area. $2,200, from $1,100 to $4,000.

rows.label: What smoke remediation of a home would cost from a contractor
rows.explainer: Our judgment: cleaning a smoke-damaged standing house of ash and soot (HEPA vacuuming, wiping every surface, cleaning the ducts, replacing filters and sealing). HomeAdvisor's guide to fire and smoke remediation gives a normal range of $3,107 to $51,243, average $27,175 (homeadvisor.com/cost/disaster-recovery/repair-fire-and-smoke-damage, retrieved 2026-11-14), which includes fire damage to the structure; smoke cleaning alone is the lower part of it; the families served were uninsured or underinsured ('With no insurance and limited assistance', annual report p. 9). $8,000, from $3,000 to $15,000.

rows.label: What a home's repairs would cost from contractors
rows.explainer: Our judgment: insulation, drywall, mud and tape, flooring, interior doors, trim, primer and paint for a flooded floor (North Carolina), or a roof, HVAC or electrical repair by contractors (Florida): $10,000 to $40,000 at contractors' prices, with materials. The volunteers' own labour is priced here, not separately. $20,000, from $8,000 to $45,000.

rows.label: Years a home's repairs last
rows.explainer: Our judgment: interior finishes and systems last one to three decades, but owners are often elderly and some homes flood again. 15, from 8 to 30. The result moves little with it: the value is spread over the same years it is discounted over.

rows.label: Value of help in kind to those served, as a share of its price
rows.explainer: The shared figure for services given in kind (@aid_value.inkind_services_vs_cash, 0.8, 0.5-1): gutting and sanitising a flooded home is what a household needs first. Households who would have done the work themselves or got it from others are in resp_counterfactual_adj, not here.

rows.label: Value of repairs in kind to the owners, as a share of their price
rows.explainer: The shared figure for housing given in kind (@aid_value.inkind_housing_vs_cash, 0.8, 0.6-0.95).

About the poorest fifth, a little above: 1.1, from 0.8 to 1.5.

rows.label: Muck and gut: log-consumption gain per person
rows.formula: resp_inkind_value * ln(1 + mg_price / household_size / baseline_consumption) * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, income_years)
rows.explainer: The service's price per person on the site's one log-income scale at the clients' own consumption.

rows.label: Mould sanitation: log-consumption gain per person
rows.formula: resp_inkind_value * ln(1 + ms_price / household_size / baseline_consumption) * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, income_years)
rows.explainer: As for the muck and guts.

rows.label: Smoke remediation: log-consumption gain per person
rows.formula: resp_inkind_value * ln(1 + sm_price / household_size / baseline_consumption) * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, income_years)
rows.explainer: As for the muck and guts.

rows.label: Repairs: log-consumption gain per person over the repairs' life
rows.formula: rep_inkind_value * ln(1 + rep_value_per_home / household_size / pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, rep_years) / baseline_consumption) * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, rep_years)
rows.explainer: The repairs' value as an even yearly flow over their years (its present value equals the price at the shared discount rate), per person, on the log scale at the clients' consumption, over those years.

rows.label: Log-consumption gain per person, all services
rows.formula: (mg_count * mg_ln_per_person + ms_count * ms_ln_per_person + sm_families * sm_ln_per_person + rep_homes * rep_ln_per_person) / households_reached
rows.explainer: The services' gains averaged over everyone served; each branch is adjusted on its own below.

rows.label: Volunteers' own life satisfaction gained, points for the year
rows.explainer: A side effect on the volunteers: purpose, belonging and skills. The shared figure for disaster-response volunteers (facts/volunteering.json): panel studies matching volunteers to similar non-volunteers find regular volunteering raises life satisfaction, mainly among the less happy (Binder and Freytag 2013); a deployment of a week or two is a light dose. 0.05 points (0-10) for the year, from 0 to 0.15.

rows.label: Volunteers' WELLBYs per person served
rows.explainer: The volunteers' WELLBYs spread over the people served, so the template's bridge row stays as it is.

rows.explainer: Not used, since deaths_averted_per_person is 0; kept so value_per_death is the site's standard row. Adults 15-49 are about 10% of US deaths over fifteen (CDC).

rows.label: Response services: units of value before adjustments
rows.formula: (mg_count * mg_ln_per_person + ms_count * ms_ln_per_person + sm_families * sm_ln_per_person) * household_size * $uov_per_ln_consumption
rows.explainer: Muck and guts, mould sanitations and smoke remediation

rows.label: Repairs: units of value before adjustments
rows.explainer: Repairs: units of value before adjustments

rows.label: Response: evidence
rows.explainer: Our judgment, validity only: the value is work at a contractor's price (no effect study needed); the counts are All Hands and Hearts' own, rounded ('800+'), and the period is the annual report's year. The judged parts (price, value in kind) are rows of their own. 0.85, from 0.7 to 1.

rows.label: Response: share that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: Our judgment: without All Hands and Hearts some households would have been helped by other voluntary groups (Samaritan's Purse, Team Rubicon, Southern Baptist Disaster Relief, Mennonite Disaster Service, the Crisis Cleanup network's members) or by insurers and FEMA's assistance; those who would have paid a contractor themselves count in full (the price saved), as do those who would have gone without or waited, with mould spreading. 0.55, from 0.3 to 0.8.

rows.label: Repairs: evidence
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the homes repaired are a judgment of their own row (rep_homes) and the value per home another; this is the remaining doubt about the work being finished to the standard priced. 0.85, from 0.6 to 1.

rows.label: Repairs: share that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: Our judgment, years brought forward and the counterfactual as one question: the owners were still in damaged homes months after the storms, after FEMA's capped grants and insurance; some would have repaired later with another group (long-term recovery groups, Habitat, SBP) or their own means. 0.5, from 0.25 to 0.8.

rows.label: Volunteers: evidence
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the volunteering studies are observational, people who volunteer differ, and a short deployment is a lighter dose than the regular volunteering studied. 0.5, from 0.2 to 0.8.

rows.label: Volunteers: share that wouldn't have volunteered anyway
rows.explainer: Our judgment: many volunteers would have gone with another disaster group without All Hands and Hearts. 0.5, from 0.2 to 0.8.

rows.label: Partners' resources as a share of All Hands and Hearts' cost
rows.explainer: Our judgment: partner organisations in Los Angeles (CORE, NDLON, the YMCA, the Pasadena Job Center: Form 990 Schedule O, line 4c), local long-term recovery groups that refer and co-fund homes, churches and towns lending space, and the governments that haul debris from the curb. All Hands and Hearts rents its own bases ($752,399 of rent), so less than for groups housed free. 10%, from 3% to 30%.

rows.label: Value of a volunteer hour
rows.explainer: The site's US value of a volunteer hour in 2025 (@united_states.volunteer_hour_value_2025, Independent Sector), the year most of the fiscal year falls in.

rows.label: Donated goods and services used in the US programmes
rows.explainer: The donated materials, legal services, transport and software, split like the spending.

rows.label: All Hands and Hearts' share of all resources behind the work
rows.explainer: Convention 2: All Hands and Hearts' cash cost over that plus partners' resources, the volunteers' unpaid hours at the US value of a volunteer hour (All Hands and Hearts houses and feeds them and pays long-term volunteers' stipends, all in its cost; volunteers pay their own travel, which is small and left out) and the donated goods and services at their stated value: about 0.6.

rows.label: Response: attribution
rows.explainer: The shared figure above.

rows.label: Repairs: attribution
rows.explainer: The shared figure above: the repairs use the same volunteers, donated materials and partners; contractors paid from All Hands and Hearts' grants are its own cost.

rows.label: Volunteers: attribution
rows.explainer: The shared figure above: the volunteers' own time is part of what gives them the gain.

rows.label: Response: work counted that wasn't finished
rows.explainer: Our judgment, for the response branch only: services counted that did not end in finished work (homes left part-done when a programme closed, rework). 0.95, from 0.85 to 1. The repairs' count is a judgment of homes finished, so they take 1.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: Our judgment: no government pays for this work in All Hands and Hearts' place; its programmes draw in volunteers and donated materials (counted in attribution), and some donors' gifts may replace others'. 1, from 0.9 to 1.05.

rows.label: Response: missing-data step
rows.explainer: Thin: the services are All Hands and Hearts' rounded counts for the annual report's year, and their value to those served (the price) is a judgment, not a measured price paid. So the shared missing-data step (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Repairs: missing-data step
rows.explainer: Thin: the number of homes repaired and their value are judgments.

rows.label: Volunteers: missing-data step
rows.explainer: Thin: the effect is a judgment from research on other volunteering.

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Our judgment, each effect with its sign: respiratory illness from mould averted by prompt muck-outs and sanitation (+); the Los Angeles programme's partner grants for cash vouchers, day-workers clearing burn zones and children's mental-health support, and its food and goods distributions (+: Form 990 Schedule O, line 4c); the Texas floods' first days (food, water, essentials and temporary housing; coordinating the spontaneous volunteers at the fire station: annual report p. 11) (+); small businesses repaired (+); site-supervisor and chainsaw training that builds response capacity (+); injuries to volunteers (-); work local contractors would have been paid for (-, small, since the clients mostly couldn't pay). Sized: the Los Angeles partner grants and distributions, about half that programme's $1.36 million (Schedule O describes them before the smoke work), valued like the services, +6%; Texas relief +3%; mould illness +3% (respiratory symptoms after flood exposure are common, but a lasting health effect of prompt clean-up is unmeasured); training and small businesses +2%; injuries and displaced contractors -1%. +13%, from -5% to +40%.
